::: callout-note
## How to use this quiz

This quiz is designed as a **formative self-assessment tool**, not as a test.

Its purpose is to help you:
- check your understanding of the key concepts from Topic 5,
- identify which types of thinking you find more difficult, and
- guide your revision before the tutorial and future assessments.

### What this quiz measures

Each question belongs to one of four categories:

- **Subject Knowledge (SK):** definitions, concepts, and facts.  
- **Analysis (AN):** understanding relationships and economic mechanisms.  
- **Problem Solving (PS):** applying concepts to new situations.  
- **Mathematical Thinking (MT):** working with equations and quantitative relationships.

Your score will be broken down by category so you can see **where** you are strong and where you need more practice.

### How to complete the quiz

- You may use your notes and the lecture materials.
- Take your time — the goal is understanding, not speed.
- Use the **Hints** if you get stuck.
- You may refresh and retry the quiz as many times as you like.

### How to interpret your results

- A low score is **not a problem** — it tells you what to focus on.
- If you score low in:
  - **SK:** revise definitions and core concepts.
  - **AN:** revisit the logic of the models and examples.
  - **PS:** practise applying concepts to new cases.
  - **MT:** practise the mathematical calculations and equations.

### About the leaderboard

The leaderboard is optional and anonymous. It exists only to make practice more engaging.  
It has **no effect** on your grade and is not used for evaluation.

The only purpose of this quiz is to support your learning.

:::

```{r}
#| echo: false
library(webexercises)
```

<!-- FEEDBACK SCRIPT: interactive quiz with self-assessment -->
```{=html}
<script>
(function () {
  // 1) Configure your Google Apps Script Web App URL here.
  //    Example: https://script.google.com/macros/s/XXXXXXXXXXXX/exec
  const ENDPOINT = "https://script.google.com/macros/s/AKfycbysCOTW2ZLw5ruYY84Y-o0zB7nt0jkowiC3OoKJSdh2OYv-ZXa_1vTb_TU4BYwcwSZ0Jw/exec";

  const norm = s => (s || "").replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();

  function getSelectedLabelText(qEl) {
    const input = qEl.querySelector('input[type="radio"]:checked');
    if (!input) return "";
    const label = input.closest('label') || document.querySelector('label[for="' + input.id + '"]');
    return label ? norm(label.textContent) : "";
  }

  function clearFeedback(qEl) {
    qEl.querySelectorAll("label").forEach(l => l.classList.remove("is-correct", "is-incorrect"));
    const line = qEl.querySelector(".quiz-feedback-line");
    if (line) {
      line.textContent = "";
      line.classList.add("hidden");
    }
  }

  function setFeedback(qEl, isCorrect) {
    const line = qEl.querySelector(".quiz-feedback-line");
    if (!line) return;
    line.textContent = isCorrect ? "Correct." : "Incorrect.";
    line.classList.remove("hidden");
  }

  async function postAttempt(payload) {
    // Do not attempt POST if ENDPOINT is not configured
    if (!ENDPOINT || ENDPOINT.includes("PASTE_YOUR_")) return;

    try {
      await fetch(ENDPOINT, {
        method: "POST",
        mode: "no-cors",
        keepalive: true,
        body: JSON.stringify(payload)
      });
    } catch (err) {
      console.warn("Could not save attempt:", err);
    }
  }

  async function loadLeaderboard(quizName) {
    const table = document.getElementById("leaderboard");
    if (!table) return;

    // If not configured, show a friendly message and stop.
    if (!ENDPOINT || ENDPOINT.includes("PASTE_YOUR_")) {
      table.innerHTML = "<tr><td>Leaderboard is not configured yet. Add your Apps Script URL in the page source.</td></tr>";
      return;
    }

    try {
      const res = await fetch(ENDPOINT, { method: "GET" });
      if (!res.ok) throw new Error("HTTP " + res.status);
      const rows = await res.json();

      // Filter for this quiz only (defensive: older rows may not have the fields)
      const filtered = (rows || []).filter(r => String(r.quiz || "") === String(quizName));

      // Keep best score per nickname
      const best = new Map();
      filtered.forEach(r => {
        const nick = String(r.nickname || "").trim();
        if (!nick) return;
        const score = Number(r.score);
        const total = Number(r.total);
        const ts = new Date(r.timestamp || 0).getTime();

        const prev = best.get(nick);
        if (!prev || score > prev.score || (score === prev.score && ts < prev.ts)) {
          best.set(nick, { nickname: nick, score, total, ts });
        }
      });

      const leaderboard = Array.from(best.values())
        .sort((a, b) => (b.score - a.score) || (a.ts - b.ts))
        .slice(0, 30);

      if (leaderboard.length === 0) {
        table.innerHTML = "<tr><td>No attempts recorded yet.</td></tr>";
      } else {
        table.innerHTML =
          "<tr><th>Rank</th><th>Nickname</th><th>Score</th></tr>" +
          leaderboard.map((r, i) =>
            "<tr><td>" + (i + 1) + "</td><td>" + String(r.nickname) + "</td><td>" + r.score + " / " + r.total + "</td></tr>"
          ).join("");
      }

      // Load and display question statistics
      await loadQuestionStats(quizName, rows);
    } catch (err) {
      table.innerHTML = "<tr><td>Could not load leaderboard.</td></tr>";
      console.warn("Leaderboard error:", err);
    }
  }

  async function loadQuestionStats(quizName, allRows) {
    const statsContainer = document.getElementById("question-stats");
    if (!statsContainer) return;

    // Filter for this quiz only
    const filtered = (allRows || []).filter(r => String(r.quiz || "") === String(quizName));

    console.log("=== DEBUGGING QUESTION STATS ===");
    console.log("Filtered rows count:", filtered.length);
    if (filtered.length > 0) {
      console.log("Sample row:", filtered[0]);
    }

    // Build a map of question index to identifier
    const questionIdentifiers = {};
    document.querySelectorAll(".mcq-we-q").forEach((qEl, idx) => {
      const questionText = qEl.querySelector("strong")?.textContent || "";
      const categoryMatch = questionText.match(/^(SK|AN|PS|MT)(\d+)/);
      if (categoryMatch) {
        questionIdentifiers[idx] = categoryMatch[1] + categoryMatch[2];
      } else {
        questionIdentifiers[idx] = "Q" + (idx + 1);
      }
    });

    console.log("Question identifiers map:", questionIdentifiers);

    // Count incorrect attempts per question
    const questionStats = {};
    filtered.forEach((row, rowIdx) => {
      let details = row.details || {};
      
      // If details is a string (JSON), parse it
      if (typeof details === "string") {
        try {
          details = JSON.parse(details);
          console.log(`Row ${rowIdx} - Parsed details from string`);
        } catch (e) {
          console.warn(`Row ${rowIdx} - Could not parse details:`, details);
          return;
        }
      }

      console.log(`Row ${rowIdx} - Processing details:`, details);

      Object.entries(details).forEach(([questionId, qData]) => {
        if (!questionStats[questionId]) {
          questionStats[questionId] = { incorrectCount: 0, totalCount: 0 };
        }
        
        questionStats[questionId].totalCount += 1;
        
        // Check if answer was incorrect (ok: 0 means incorrect)
        const isIncorrect = qData.ok === 0;
        if (isIncorrect) {
          questionStats[questionId].incorrectCount += 1;
        }
      });
    });

    console.log("\nFinal question stats:", questionStats);

    // Get top 10 most incorrect questions, sorted by incorrect count
    const sortedQuestions = Object.entries(questionStats)
      .map(([qKey, stats]) => ({
        qKey: qKey,
        incorrectCount: stats.incorrectCount,
        totalCount: stats.totalCount,
        incorrectRate: stats.totalCount > 0 ? (stats.incorrectCount / stats.totalCount * 100).toFixed(1) : 0
      }))
      .sort((a, b) => b.incorrectCount - a.incorrectCount)
      .slice(0, 10);

    console.log("Sorted questions:", sortedQuestions);

    if (sortedQuestions.length === 0) {
      statsContainer.innerHTML = "<p>No question statistics available yet.</p>";
    } else {
      statsContainer.innerHTML =
        "<h4>Top 10 Questions with Most Incorrect Attempts</h4>" +
        "<table style='width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse;'>" +
        "<tr style='border-bottom: 2px solid #ccc;'><th style='text-align: left; padding: 8px;'>Question</th><th style='text-align: center; padding: 8px;'>Incorrect Attempts</th><th style='text-align: center; padding: 8px;'>Total Attempts</th><th style='text-align: center; padding: 8px;'>Incorrect Rate</th></tr>" +
        sortedQuestions.map(q =>
          "<tr style='border-bottom: 1px solid #eee;'>" +
          "<td style='padding: 8px;'>" + String(q.qKey) + "</td>" +
          "<td style='text-align: center; padding: 8px;'>" + q.incorrectCount + "</td>" +
          "<td style='text-align: center; padding: 8px;'>" + q.totalCount + "</td>" +
          "<td style='text-align: center; padding: 8px;'>" + q.incorrectRate + "%</td>" +
          "</tr>"
        ).join("") +
        "</table>";
    }
  }

  async function submitQuiz() {
    const nicknameEl = document.getElementById("nickname");
    const resultEl = document.getElementById("quiz-result");
    const submitBtn = document.getElementById("quiz-submit");

    const nickname = (nicknameEl?.value || "").trim();
    if (!nickname) {
      alert("Please enter a nickname before submitting.");
      nicknameEl?.focus();
      return;
    }

    // Lock submit to avoid double posting
    if (submitBtn) submitBtn.disabled = true;

    let score = 0;
    let total = 0;
    const details = {};
    
    // Category scores
    const categories = {
      SK: { score: 0, total: 0, name: "Subject Knowledge" },
      AN: { score: 0, total: 0, name: "Analysis" },
      PS: { score: 0, total: 0, name: "Problem Solving" },
      MT: { score: 0, total: 0, name: "Mathematical Thinking" }
    };

    const questions = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll(".mcq-we-q"));

    // Clear any prior feedback first (important if student re-submits)
    questions.forEach(clearFeedback);

    questions.forEach((qEl, idx) => {
      total += 1;
      const keyEl = qEl.querySelector(".mcq-key");
      const correct = norm(keyEl?.getAttribute("data-correct") || "");
      const selected = getSelectedLabelText(qEl);

      const isCorrect = selected && (selected === correct);
      if (isCorrect) score += 1;

      // Extract category and question ID from question text (SK1, AN1, PS1, MT1, etc.)
      const questionText = qEl.querySelector("strong")?.textContent || "";
      const categoryMatch = questionText.match(/^(SK|AN|PS|MT)(\d+)/);
      let questionId = "Q" + (idx + 1);
      
      if (categoryMatch) {
        const cat = categoryMatch[1];
        const num = categoryMatch[2];
        questionId = cat + num;
        
        categories[cat].total += 1;
        if (isCorrect) categories[cat].score += 1;
      }

      details[questionId] = { selected, correct, ok: isCorrect ? 1 : 0 };

      // Mark only after submit
      if (selected) {
        const input = qEl.querySelector('input[type="radio"]:checked');
        const label = input?.closest("label") || (input ? document.querySelector('label[for="' + input.id + '"]') : null);
        if (label) label.classList.add(isCorrect ? "is-correct" : "is-incorrect");
      }
      setFeedback(qEl, isCorrect);
    });

    if (resultEl) {
      let resultHTML = "<strong>Overall Score: " + score + " / " + total + "</strong><br><br>";
      
      // Add category breakdown
      for (const key in categories) {
        const cat = categories[key];
        if (cat.total > 0) {
          resultHTML += cat.name + ": " + cat.score + " / " + cat.total + "<br>";
        }
      }
      
      // Add correct and incorrect questions
      const correctQuestions = [];
      const incorrectQuestions = [];
      
      questions.forEach((qEl, idx) => {
        const keyEl = qEl.querySelector(".mcq-key");
        const correct = norm(keyEl?.getAttribute("data-correct") || "");
        const selected = getSelectedLabelText(qEl);
        const isCorrect = selected && (selected === correct);
        
        // Extract question ID from question text
        const questionText = qEl.querySelector("strong")?.textContent || "";
        const categoryMatch = questionText.match(/^(SK|AN|PS|MT)(\d+)/);
        let questionId = "Q" + (idx + 1);
        if (categoryMatch) {
          questionId = categoryMatch[1] + categoryMatch[2];
        }
        
        if (selected) {
          if (isCorrect) {
            correctQuestions.push(questionId);
          } else {
            incorrectQuestions.push(questionId);
          }
        }
      });
      
      resultHTML += "<br><strong>Correct Questions:</strong> " + (correctQuestions.length > 0 ? correctQuestions.join(", ") : "None") + "<br>";
      resultHTML += "<strong>Incorrect Questions:</strong> " + (incorrectQuestions.length > 0 ? incorrectQuestions.join(", ") : "None") + "<br>";
      
      resultEl.innerHTML = resultHTML;
    }

    // Persist attempt (best practice: store what you need; nickname only = low GDPR footprint)
    await postAttempt({
      timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
      nickname,
      quiz: "Topic5",
      score,
      total,
      details
    });

    // Refresh leaderboard after a successful submit (or best-effort submit)
    await loadLeaderboard("Topic5");

    // Disable all radio buttons and submit button to prevent further changes
    document.querySelectorAll(".mcq-we-q input[type='radio']").forEach(input => {
      input.disabled = true;
    });
    if (submitBtn) submitBtn.disabled = true;
  }

  // Expose submitQuiz globally for the button onclick
  window.submitQuiz = submitQuiz;

  // Add a feedback line container to each question if it doesn't exist
  document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {
    document.querySelectorAll(".mcq-we-q").forEach(qEl => {
      if (!qEl.querySelector(".quiz-feedback-line")) {
        const line = document.createElement("div");
        line.className = "quiz-feedback-line hidden";
        qEl.appendChild(line);
      }
    });

    loadLeaderboard("Topic5");
  });
})();
</script>
```

## Subject Knowledge

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**SK1) In the New Keynesian framework, the central bank typically sets:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("The money supply directly", answer = "The nominal interest rate", "The real wage", "Government spending"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="The nominal interest rate"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Modern monetary policy is usually described in terms of an instrument rule rather than money quantities.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**SK2) The New Keynesian IS curve primarily relates:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Inflation and unemployment", "Output and the nominal interest rate", answer = "Output and the real interest rate", "Money supply and prices"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Output and the real interest rate"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Intertemporal consumption decisions depend on real borrowing costs.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**SK3) In the New Keynesian Phillips Curve (NKPC), inflation depends on:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Past inflation only", answer = "Expected future inflation and marginal cost", "Money growth alone", "Government deficits"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Expected future inflation and marginal cost"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Forward-looking price-setting is central to the Calvo framework.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**SK4) The output gap is defined as:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Actual output minus government spending", "Potential output minus inflation", answer = "Actual output minus natural output", "Inflation minus expected inflation"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Actual output minus natural output"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Distinguish cyclical deviations from supply-determined output.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**SK5) Price stickiness in New Keynesian models is often formalised using:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Adaptive expectations", "Rational bubbles", answer = "Calvo pricing", "Quantity theory"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Calvo pricing"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Only a fraction of firms adjust prices in each period.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**SK6) The Taylor rule links the policy rate to:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Money growth and velocity", answer = "Inflation and the output gap", "Unemployment and fiscal deficits", "Exchange rates only"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Inflation and the output gap"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>The rule responds systematically to deviations from targets.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**SK7) The natural real rate of interest is the rate that:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Maximises inflation", "Eliminates money demand", answer = "Keeps output at potential", "Sets velocity constant"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Keeps output at potential"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>It is the equilibrium rate consistent with zero output gap.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**SK8) At the effective lower bound (ELB), conventional policy is constrained because:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Inflation cannot rise", answer = "Nominal interest rates cannot fall much below zero", "Real output becomes fixed", "Velocity becomes constant"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Nominal interest rates cannot fall much below zero"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Consider institutional limits on nominal rates.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**SK9) Forward guidance works primarily by influencing:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Current money supply", answer = "Expected future policy rates", "Government taxation", "Labour supply"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Expected future policy rates"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Expectations of future policy affect current long-term rates.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**SK10) In the canonical 3-equation New Keynesian model, monetary policy affects output in the short run mainly through:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Real wage rigidity", answer = "The real interest rate channel", "Permanent productivity shifts", "Fiscal multipliers"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="The real interest rate channel"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Track how nominal rates translate into intertemporal substitution.</details>
</div>

## Analysis

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**AN1) If expected inflation rises while the nominal policy rate is unchanged, what happens to the real interest rate?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("It rises", answer = "It falls", "It stays constant", "It becomes zero"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="It falls"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Use the Fisher decomposition to separate nominal and real components.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**AN2) Why does price stickiness generate a short-run output response to monetary policy?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Because money directly determines productivity", answer = "Because nominal rigidities prevent immediate price adjustment", "Because velocity is unstable", "Because fiscal policy dominates"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Because nominal rigidities prevent immediate price adjustment"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Compare flexible-price neutrality with rigid-price dynamics.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**AN3) If the central bank raises rates more than one-for-one with inflation (Taylor principle), what is stabilised?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Velocity", "The money supply", answer = "Inflation expectations", "Fiscal deficits"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Inflation expectations"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Consider determinacy conditions in rational expectations models.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**AN4) Why does a negative demand shock lower both output and inflation in the NK model?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Because productivity rises", answer = "Because marginal cost falls", "Because money supply shrinks mechanically", "Because velocity doubles"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Because marginal cost falls"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Link the output gap to real marginal cost in the Phillips curve.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**AN5) If the central bank keeps rates too low relative to the natural rate, the output gap will likely be:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Negative", "Zero", answer = "Positive", "Undefined"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Positive"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Compare the policy rate with the equilibrium real rate.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**AN6) At the ELB, why can forward guidance stimulate current demand?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("It increases productivity", answer = "It lowers expected future real interest rates", "It raises taxes", "It fixes inflation at zero"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="It lowers expected future real interest rates"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Expectations about future borrowing costs affect current spending decisions.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**AN7) If firms expect lower future marginal costs, what happens to current inflation?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("It rises", answer = "It falls", "It is unaffected", "It becomes negative permanently"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="It falls"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>The NKPC is forward-looking.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**AN8) Why is the Taylor principle necessary for a unique equilibrium?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("To eliminate money", answer = "To prevent self-fulfilling inflation paths", "To stabilise fiscal deficits", "To ensure velocity constancy"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="To prevent self-fulfilling inflation paths"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Think about how expectations can generate multiple equilibria.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**AN9) If fiscal policy persistently raises demand without monetary accommodation, what must happen to interest rates under a Taylor rule?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("They fall", "They remain unchanged", answer = "They rise", "They become negative"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="They rise"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Apply the rule mechanically to higher inflation/output gap.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**AN10) Why does the NK model reject strict long-run money neutrality as a policy guide in the short run?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Because prices are flexible", answer = "Because nominal rigidities create real effects", "Because velocity is constant", "Because unemployment is irrelevant"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Because nominal rigidities create real effects"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Separate long-run neutrality from short-run non-neutrality.</details>
</div>

## Problem Solving

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**PS1) Inflation rises above target while the output gap is positive. According to a Taylor rule, the central bank should:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Cut rates", answer = "Raise rates", "Fix money supply", "Do nothing"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Raise rates"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Consider how the rule responds to deviations in both arguments.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**PS2) The natural real rate is 1%, expected inflation is 2%, and the central bank sets the nominal rate at 2%. What is the real policy rate?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c(answer = "0%", "1%", "2%", "3%"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="0%"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Subtract expected inflation from the nominal rate.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**PS3) A negative technology shock raises marginal cost. What happens immediately to inflation?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("It falls", answer = "It rises", "It is unchanged", "It becomes zero"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="It rises"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Use the cost channel in the Phillips curve.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**PS4) If the central bank credibly commits to keeping rates low for longer, what happens to long-term interest rates?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("They rise", answer = "They fall", "They are unchanged", "They double"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="They fall"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Long-term rates reflect expected future short rates.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**PS5) The economy is at the ELB and faces a negative demand shock. The central bank announces future overshooting of inflation. Why might this stimulate demand today?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("It raises expected future real rates", answer = "It lowers expected future real rates", "It eliminates marginal cost", "It fixes output permanently"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="It lowers expected future real rates"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Think intertemporally about expected inflation.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**PS6) If the real rate exceeds the natural rate, what happens to the output gap over time?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("It becomes positive", "It remains zero", answer = "It becomes negative", "It becomes undefined"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="It becomes negative"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Compare borrowing costs to equilibrium conditions.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**PS7) A positive demand shock raises output above potential. What happens to inflation over time if policy does not respond strongly enough?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("It declines", "It stabilises immediately", answer = "It rises persistently", "It disappears"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="It rises persistently"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Use the forward-looking Phillips curve and weak policy response.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**PS8) If the central bank violates the Taylor principle, what risk arises?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Guaranteed stability", answer = "Multiple equilibria", "Permanent zero inflation", "Elimination of output fluctuations"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Multiple equilibria"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Consider determinacy under rational expectations.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**PS9) A permanent increase in the natural real rate occurs, but the policy rate does not adjust. What happens to the output gap?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("It becomes positive", answer = "It becomes negative", "It stays zero", "It vanishes"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="It becomes negative"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Compare the stance of policy relative to equilibrium.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**PS10) Why can credible commitment to a future inflation overshoot help escape a liquidity trap?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("It raises current real interest rates", answer = "It lowers current real interest rates", "It fixes velocity", "It eliminates the output gap instantly"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="It lowers current real interest rates"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Expectations of higher inflation reduce real borrowing costs today.</details>
</div>

## Mathematical Thinking

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT1) Using $i = r + \pi^e$, if $r=1%$ and $\pi^e=3%$, then $i$ equals:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("2%", "3%", answer = "4%", "5%"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="4%"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Add the two components.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT2) If the output gap is $x_t = Y_t - Y_t^* = 2$, what does this imply?**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Output below potential", answer = "Output above potential", "Zero inflation", "Negative inflation"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Output above potential"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Check the sign of the deviation.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT3) Given $\pi_t = \beta E_t[\pi_{t+1}] + \kappa x_t$, if $x_t=0$, inflation equals:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Zero", answer = "beta E_t[pi_{t+1}]", "kappa", "The natural rate"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="beta E_t[pi_{t+1}]"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Substitute carefully when the output gap is zero.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT4) If $\kappa$ increases, the Phillips curve becomes:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Flatter", answer = "Steeper", "Vertical", "Horizontal"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Steeper"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Consider the responsiveness of inflation to the output gap.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT5) Under the Taylor rule $i_t = r^* + \pi_t + 0.5(\pi_t-\pi^*) + 0.5x_t$, if inflation rises above target, $i_t$ will:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Fall", answer = "Rise", "Stay constant", "Become negative"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Rise"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Focus on the deviation term.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT6) If the Taylor coefficient on inflation is less than 1, the real rate response to higher inflation is:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Positive", answer = "Negative", "Zero", "Infinite"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Negative"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Compare nominal adjustment to inflation change.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT7) If expected inflation rises by 2pp and nominal rates rise by 1pp, the real rate:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Rises by 1pp", answer = "Falls by 1pp", "Is unchanged", "Doubles"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Falls by 1pp"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Subtract expected inflation from nominal rates.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT8) In $x_t = E_t[x_{t+1}] - \sigma (i_t - E_t\pi_{t+1} - r^*)$, if $i_t - E_t\pi_{t+1} > r^*$, then $x_t$:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Increases", answer = "Decreases", "Is zero", "Becomes constant"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Decreases"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Examine the sign of the bracketed term.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT9) If $\beta=0.99$, higher credibility (raising $\beta$ toward 1) makes inflation more:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Backward-looking", answer = "Forward-looking", "Random", "Independent of expectations"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Forward-looking"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Interpret the weight on expected future inflation.</details>
</div>

<div class="mcq-we-q">
**MT10) If the central bank raises $i_t$ more than one-for-one with inflation, the real rate response is:**  
`r webexercises::longmcq(c("Negative", "Zero", answer = "Positive", "Undefined"))`
<span class="mcq-key" data-correct="Positive"></span>
<details class="hint"><summary>Hint</summary>Apply the Taylor principle algebraically.</details>
</div>
